findings.what: The piece sets its own register: listen.reg, one value per crossing (octaves from D5), used by harpStep in place of ln|F| when the guard passes. The melody file's register block: centre = log2(f/D5) + 0.75 for each written main note (graces take their main note's, the coda -0.45), so the loudest octave copy is always the written note an octave up (B4 to B5) and never flips at a bar line. The guide says 'This example sets its own register and dynamics.'
findings.evidence: t_seasong: 'the loudest copy follows the written contour': 66 steps of the theme, 0 flipped (F#->E is a step down, F#->B a fourth up, B->A a step down); the margin is 4.4 dB, above a string's random +-1 dB, and the check passed on 7 runs with different seeds. A first try with the range compressed to 0.8 flipped 2 steps on one seed, so it was dropped. The per-statement rise the review suggested was dropped for the same reason: the theme's B3..B4 already fills the harp's whole register range.

findings.what: Graces in the background: a passing grace 0.12x its main note, the turn's re-pluck (the string just played) 0.08x, a D grace x0.6 more, the flam 0. findings.evidence: 9 silent crossings (3 flams, the coda's 6 E/A); 150 of 159 crossings sound; t_seasong 'graces at most 0.12 of the note they lead to' (0.121 after rounding). The crossings, their order, directions and onsets are unchanged (worst 7.2 ms in node, 7.5 ms recorded).

findings.what: The drum follows the dynamics: listen.tick holds one gain per cut tick, 20 log10(v/0.9) dB with v the main note on that beat (-6.5 dB rising to +0.9 dB), used when the tick count matches. A piece's tick is a single pluck (cut make: o.one), without the repetition softening, so a downbeat is the B plus one tick.

findings.what: The corners are fixed. The 1200 stored points are now spread by arc length and turning angle (pointsBy.turn 0.6) from the generator's fine solution, so the hairpins get more points. The self-crossings are not fixed. They come from F: with z^(-1+i b) and two turns per statement, a radial excursion of D turns of arg F reaches 2D ring spacings, whatever b is. Every leap of more than half a turn (A F# D, for example) must cross the next turn. Removing the crossings means a different F, for example z^(-2+i b) with one turn per statement, and that loses the drum on the downbeats of bars 1 and 3. This is the design choice the review asks the user to make.
findings.evidence: Largest turn between neighbouring stored points: 29.6 -> 11.2 degrees; vertices over 12 degrees: 83 -> 0; vertices over 20 degrees: 28 -> 0. Segment length 0.002 to 0.08 (17 px at s = 215, on the nearly straight parts). Self-crossings: 27 -> 31 (the finer hairpins show crossings the coarse polyline cut through; the curve itself is unchanged). t_seasong's sampling sweep still gives the same 159 crossings (8 sample counts x 3 point sets).
